# 1 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

1. In those days Mattathias son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
2. He had five sons: John, called Gaddi;
3. Simon, called Thassi;
4. Judas, who was called Maccabeus;
5. Eleazar, called Avaran; and Jonathan, called Apphus.
6. When he saw the blasphemies being committed in Judah and in Jerusalem,
7. he said, "Woe is me! Why was I born to see this — the destruction of my people and the ruin of the holy city — and to sit idle while she is given into the hands of enemies, the sanctuary into the hands of foreigners?
8. Her temple has become like a man stripped of honor.
9. The precious vessels of her glory have been carried into exile; her infants have been killed in her streets, her young men by the sword of the enemy.
10. What nation has not taken its share of her royal precincts and seized her spoils?
11. All her adornment has been stripped away. Once free, she has become a slave.
12. Look — our holy things, our beauty, our glory have all been laid waste, and the Gentiles have profaned them.
13. Why then should we live any longer?"
14. Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned bitterly.
15. The king's officers who were enforcing the apostasy came to the town of Modein to compel them to sacrifice.
16. Many of the people of Israel came to them; and Mattathias and his sons came together.
17. The king's officers said to Mattathias: "You are a leader, a distinguished and great man in this city, supported by sons and brothers.
18. Come now, be the first to carry out the king's command, as all the Gentiles and the people of Judah and those who remain in Jerusalem have done; then you and your sons will be among the friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honored with silver and gold and many gifts."
19. But Mattathias answered in a loud voice: "Even if every nation within the king's dominion obeys him and every man abandons the religion of his fathers and chooses to follow his commands,
20. yet I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
21. Heaven forbid that we should abandon the Torah and its ordinances.
22. We will not obey the king's words by turning aside from our worship, either to the right or to the left."
23. When he had finished speaking, one of the men of Israel stepped forward in the sight of all and sacrificed on the altar in Modein, in compliance with the king's command.
24. When Mattathias saw it, he burned with zeal and his heart was stirred; in righteous indignation he ran forward and slaughtered the man upon the altar.
25. At the same time he also killed the king's officer who was compelling them to sacrifice, and he tore down the altar.
26. He acted with zeal for the Torah, just as Phinehas had done against Zimri son of Salu.
27. Then Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice: "Let everyone who is zealous for the Torah and who stands by the covenant come out and follow me!"
28. He and his sons fled to the hills and abandoned everything they had in the city.
29. At that time many who were seeking righteousness and justice went down to the wilderness to live there —
30. they, their sons, their wives, and their livestock — because evil had grown so great against them.
31. Word was brought to the king's officers and the forces in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had rejected the king's command had gone down to the hiding places in the wilderness.
32. Many went in pursuit and overtook them; they made camp against them and prepared to attack on the sabbath day.
33. They called out to them: "Come out at once and do as the king commands, and you will live."
34. They replied, "We will not come out, and we will not do the king's command to profane the sabbath day."
35. Then the enemy hastened to attack them.
36. But the men offered no resistance; they threw no stones, blocked no entrances,
37. but said: "Let us all die with a clear conscience. Heaven and earth are witnesses against you that you are killing us unjustly."
38. So they attacked on the sabbath day, and they died — men, wives, children, and livestock — about a thousand persons.
39. When Mattathias and his companions heard of this, they mourned deeply for them.
40. And each said to his neighbor: "If we all act as our brothers have acted, and refuse to fight the Gentiles for our lives and our ordinances, they will soon wipe us off the face of the earth."
41. That very day they came to this decision: "If anyone attacks us on the sabbath day, let us fight back, so that we do not all die as our brothers died in the hiding places."
42. Then a group of the Hasideans joined them — mighty men of Israel, every man who had given himself willingly to the Torah.
43. All who were fleeing from the evils joined them and reinforced them.
44. They organized their forces and struck down sinners in their anger and lawless men in their fury; the survivors fled to the Gentiles.
45. Mattathias and his friends went throughout the region tearing down the pagan altars.
46. They forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised boys they found within the borders of Israel.
47. They drove the arrogant before them, and the work went forward in their hands.
48. They recovered the Torah from the hands of the Gentiles and the kings, and they never let the sinner gain the upper hand.
49. When the time came for Mattathias to die, he said to his sons: "Arrogance and contempt have now grown strong; it is a time of ruin and furious anger.
50. Now, my sons, be zealous for the Torah and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
51. Call to mind what our fathers did in their time, and you will receive great honor and an everlasting name.
52. Was not Abraham found faithful under trial, and was it not counted to him as righteousness?
53. Joseph, in his time of distress, kept the commandment, and so he became lord of Egypt.
54. Phinehas our father, for his burning zeal, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
55. Joshua, because he fulfilled his assigned duty, became a judge in Israel.
56. Caleb, because he gave a true report in the assembly, received an inheritance in the land.
57. David, because he was compassionate, inherited the throne of the kingdom forever.
58. Elijah, because of his burning zeal for the Torah, was taken up into heaven.
59. Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael trusted in God and were saved from the flame.
60. Daniel, because of his integrity, was delivered from the mouth of the lions.
61. So consider this, generation after generation: all who put their hope in him will not fail in strength.
62. Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory will turn to dung and worms.
63. Today he is exalted; tomorrow he is nowhere to be found, for he has returned to the dust, and his scheming has come to nothing.
64. My sons, be courageous and strong in the Torah, for through it you shall win glory.
65. Here is your brother Simon — I know him to be a man of wise counsel. Listen to him all your days; he shall be a father to you.
66. And Judas Maccabeus, who has been strong and mighty from his youth — let him be your commander and lead the campaign of the people.
67. Gather to yourselves all who observe the Torah, and exact vengeance for your people.
68. Pay back the Gentiles what they deserve and hold fast to the commandments of the Torah."
69. Then he blessed them and was gathered to his ancestors.
70. He died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tomb of his fathers at Modein, and all Israel made great lamentation over him.
